reuse: Monday does the heavy lifting for two nights. Buy the full 6 lb pork shoulder — about 2.5 lb of the pulled meat gets pocketed before dinner hits the table and becomes Wednesday's bánh mì bowls, crisped in a dry skillet so it eats like a new dish instead of leftovers. While the pork rests Monday, cook 4 cups of dry jasmine rice: Tuesday's side and Wednesday's bowls both come out of that one pot, so Wednesday cooks no protein and no grain at all. One head of cabbage and one bag of carrots split between Monday's slaw and Wednesday's quick pickle. One zucchini buy covers Tuesday's skillet and Thursday's roasting pan, and the lemons, butter and mayonnaise each span two nights. No corn, no beans anywhere this week.

dinners.name: Crispy Oven Pulled Pork with Cabbage Slaw
dinners.blurb: Slow-roasted pork shoulder with a sweet-smoky bark, pulled into a tangy cider mop and piled on rolls with crunchy cabbage-carrot slaw.
dinners.warn: Two-part timing. The rub goes on SUNDAY NIGHT, and the roast needs ~5 hours at 300°F — so it has to be in the oven by 12:30 PM for a 6 PM dinner. If nobody is home midday, roast it Sunday afternoon instead and rewarm 10 min at 450°F Monday.

items: 6 lb boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt) — 6 to 8 lb is fine, bigger is better
1/4 cup + 1 Tbsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (Morton's: use 3 Tbsp)
1 head green cabbage (~2 lb) — save a quarter for Wednesday
1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more to taste
Hot sauce on the side (keeps the roast itself mild for the kids)

directions: SUNDAY NIGHT: mix the salt, 7 Tbsp brown sugar, smoked paprika and chipotle. Score the fat cap in a 1/8-inch-deep diamond pattern. Pat the rub thickly onto every side of the pork. Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.
Make the mop: whisk the cider vinegar, ketchup, 3 Tbsp brown sugar, black pepper and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves. Makes about 2 1/2 cups. Keeps in the fridge.
MONDAY, by 12:30 PM: heat oven to 300°F. Unwrap the pork, pour off any accumulated juices, set it in a roasting pan and put it in.

After the first hour, add 1/4 cup of mop to the pan juices and baste. Baste again every hour with whatever has collected in the pan. Roast about 5 hours total (a 6 lb roast may want 5 1/2), until the meat collapses and yields easily to a fork.
Let it rest — it can sit at room temperature up to 1 1/2 hours. Shred with two forks, discarding the big chunks of fat. Pour up to 3/4 cup of mop over the shredded meat to season and moisten it.
↻ RESERVE NOW, BEFORE IT HITS THE TABLE: pull about 2.5 lb of the shredded pork into a container and refrigerate it. That is Wednesday's dinner, and it will not survive the table if you leave it out.

Slaw: quarter, core and thinly slice about three quarters of the cabbage (save the rest for Wednesday). Toss with the shredded carrots and 1/3 cup of the mop, then mix in the mayonnaise. Salt and pepper to taste.

↻ ALSO TONIGHT, while the pork rests: cook 4 cups dry jasmine rice (4 cups rice + 6 cups water, covered, boil then 15 min on low, then 15 min off-heat still covered). Cool and refrigerate. Tuesday's side and Wednesday's bowls both come out of this pot.
Serve on rolls with slaw and the remaining mop. Hot sauce on the table.
dinners.reuse: Buy the full 6 lb — ~2.5 lb of pulled pork becomes Wednesday's bánh mì bowls, so Wednesday cooks no protein at all. Tonight's 4 cups of dry rice feeds Tuesday's side AND Wednesday's bowls. The cabbage head and carrot bag also carry into Wednesday's quick pickle.
dinners.alt: Shredded crispy oven pulled pork piled on a soft roll with pale cabbage slaw

dinners.name: Blackened Salmon with Zucchini
dinners.blurb: Salmon crusted in homemade Cajun spice and hard-seared until the crust goes dark, with zucchini sautéed in the spiced butter left in the pan.

ingredients.group: Cajun seasoning (double batch — this is the whole mix)

items: 2 1/4 lb salmon, skin removed, cut into 5 portions (~7 oz each)
2 1/2 lb zucchini (about 5 medium), sliced into half-rounds
About 4 cups of Monday's cooked jasmine rice

directions: Stir all the Cajun seasoning spices together in a small bowl.
Cut the salmon into 5 equal portions and coat generously on all sides with the seasoning. Use all of it — a thin dusting will not blacken.
Slice the zucchini into half-rounds and set aside.
Reheat Monday's rice: 4 cups into a saucepan with a splash of water, covered, low heat, ~8 min. Or microwave covered.

Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high until foaming. Add the salmon — work in two batches so the pieces are not crowded, or the crust steams instead of searing. Cook 5-7 min per side, until a dark crust forms and the center hits 145°F.
Move the salmon to a plate. Add the zucchini to the same skillet and sauté in the residual spiced butter until tender, 5-6 min. Scrape up the browned bits — that is where the flavor is.
Serve immediately over the rice with lemon wedges. Squeeze the lemon; it is what makes the blackening taste like something instead of just hot.
dinners.reuse: The rice is Monday's — nothing to cook. The zucchini comes out of the same buy as Thursday's pasta, and the lemons and butter are shared with Thursday too.
dinners.alt: Dark-crusted blackened salmon fillet flaked open beside sautéed zucchini half-rounds

dinners.name: Bánh Mì Bowls with Monday's Pulled Pork
dinners.blurb: Everything good about a bánh mì sandwich, in a bowl: crisped pork over jasmine rice with sweet-sour pickled carrot and cabbage, cool cucumber, a fistful of cilantro and sriracha mayo.
dinners.warn: Adapted: the original builds these on baked pork meatballs. We use Monday's pulled pork instead — bánh mì is a pork sandwich, so this is the swap the dish wants anyway. Make the pickle Monday night or Tuesday; it needs at least 30 min in the fridge.

items: About 2 cups shredded green cabbage (the quarter head left from Monday)
~2.5 lb pulled pork reserved from Monday
About 8 cups cooked jasmine rice from Monday's pot
1 English cucumber, quartered lengthwise and sliced
2 jalapeños, sliced thin — ON THE SIDE
1/2 bunch cilantro, leaves pulled from the stems
2 Tbsp sriracha, plus more to taste

directions: MAKE THE PICKLE AHEAD (Monday night or Tuesday, or at least 30 min before dinner): combine the rice vinegar, sugar, salt and water in a small pot and warm just until the sugar dissolves. Let it cool. Shred the carrots and cabbage, slice the onion thin, and pack them into a container. Pour the liquid over, making sure everything is submerged. Refrigerate — it only gets better through Thursday.
Reheat the rice: 8 cups into a large saucepan with a splash of water, covered, low heat, ~10 min, fluffing once. Or microwave covered in two batches.

Crisp the pork — this is the step that makes it a new meal instead of leftovers. Heat a dry large skillet over medium-high. Spread the pork in a single layer and leave it alone 3-4 min until the underside browns and crackles, then toss and repeat once. Work in two batches; a crowded pan steams.
Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together.
Prep the cold stuff: slice the cucumber into quarter-rounds, slice the jalapeños, pull the cilantro leaves.
Build: ~1 1/2 cups rice in each bowl, a generous pile of crisped pork, 1/2 cup of the drained pickle, cucumber, a real handful of cilantro. Zigzag the sriracha mayo over the top.
Jalapeños and extra sriracha stay on the table so everyone dials their own heat.
dinners.reuse: This night cooks no protein and no grain — the pork and the rice both came out of Monday. The carrots and cabbage are the back half of Monday's slaw buy, and the mayo jar is the same one.
dinners.alt: Overhead bánh mì bowl of rice topped with pork, pickled carrot, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño

dinners.name: Cherry Tomato & Summer Squash Pasta with Chicken Sausage
dinners.blurb: Cherry tomatoes roasted until they burst, with zucchini and yellow squash, tossed through whole-grain pasta in a light goat cheese and lemon sauce. Italian chicken sausage added so it actually holds as a dinner.

items: 1 lb whole grain rotini, fusilli or penne
3 medium yellow squash, quartered lengthwise and sliced into 1/4-inch wedges
2 medium zucchini, quartered lengthwise and sliced into 1/4-inch wedges
2 small cloves garlic, pressed or minced
Generous pinch red pepper flakes — ON THE SIDE for the kids' portions
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment. Toss the cherry tomatoes, zucchini and yellow squash with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer — use two sheets if it looks crowded, because piled vegetables steam instead of roasting. Roast 25 min, stirring halfway, until the tomatoes burst and the squash is tender.
While that roasts, sear the sausage: brown the links in a skillet over medium, 10-12 min, turning, until cooked through. Rest 5 min, then slice into coins on the bias.
Boil a large pot of well-salted water and cook the pasta to al dente per the package. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining, then return the pasta to the pot.

While the pasta is still hot, add the lemon juice, butter, goat cheese, garlic and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Add 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta water and toss gently until everything is coated and glossy. Add more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks tight — the goat cheese is the sauce, so it needs the starch water to loosen.
Add the roasted vegetables and every drop of the juices from the pan, plus the sliced sausage. Toss gently. Taste and correct the salt and pepper.
Top with the chopped basil and serve immediately. Extra red pepper flakes and grated parmesan on the table.
dinners.reuse: The zucchini and lemons come out of Tuesday's buy, and the butter is the same stick. Basil and goat cheese are the only things bought just for tonight.
dinners.alt: Bowl of rotini tossed with burst cherry tomatoes, roasted summer squash and crumbled goat cheese
